newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Shell Sri Lanka strike hits supply.
newsitem.headline: Shell Sri Lanka strike hits supply.

text.p: A three-day strike at Sri Lanka's monopoly gas distributor, owned by the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, has crippled distribution, a company spokesman said on Monday.

"The supply situation is pretty critical," he said. "We're begining to get a situation where a lot of dealers do not have stocks and there's severe pressure from industrial users who have very low stock levels."
The company's two main plants near Colombo had stopped supplying gas but two centres in southern Galle and Kandy, in the central hills, were still filling cylinders of consumers, he said.

The strike was launched on Friday by workers of the All Ceylon Commercial and Industrial Workers Union demanding an immediate halt to transfers of employees and the reinstatement of six workers who were dismissed.
The company spokesman said Labour Commissioner R.P. Wimalasena will hold talks later on Monday with the labour union and company officials to try to end the strike.
A ship with 1,750 tonnes of gas has been waiting outside Colombo port since Saturday, unable to unload because of the strike, he said.
This is the second strike at the company since it was privatised in October 1995.

A six-day strike by union labour, demanding the reinstatement of nine workers suspended for violating safety rules at Colombo port when unloading gas, brought gas distribution to a halt in the Indian Ocean island last November.
